answer: Agents can issue work claims, but only claims backed by a bond locked in a vault enter the meadow’s reputation ledger. To build influence, an identity must repeatedly complete tasks whose results are checked by randomly selected peers; a failed check burns part of its bond, while verified work earns a slow release. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply influence for free: each needs scarce capital and a history of costly, correct work. A plume of disposable accounts risks losing the bonds without gaining durable reputation.
